A visible Feed/Home may own exactly one data-ready autoplay video; the 3D Map may retain its parked WebGL state but may not keep drawing or accumulating heap. RECALIBRATED 2026-08-15: the gate now measures the BUILT SNAPSHOT being published (sync-mobile serves it on a loopback port) instead of the 5199 dev server. Dev home/feed never mount the real 3D surfaces (forceMapLoading is DEV-only), so the old home/feed numbers were calibrated against pages missing three WebGL contexts and their idle CPU. New home/feed baselines = the last accepted SHIPPED bundle (iOS ClayMapWeb, measured 2026-08-15: webgl 7, home 291ms / feed 323ms min renderer CPU) via the original max(250, round(threadMs*1.5)) formula. Map budgets unchanged — the production map passes its dev-era budgets (webgl 4, ~60-108ms). ARRIVAL BUDGETS ADDED 2026-08-21: every budget above measured a SETTLED surface, so per-visit warm-up cost was invisible — a surface could pass this gate and still cook the phone through repeated visits. maxArrivalCpuMs bounds renderer-thread CPU in the first 30s after mount. Calibrating it immediately showed why it was needed: the gated `map` (front=0, no cinematic intro) arrives for ~1.8s, while the front=1 map users actually get costs ~5.9-7.5s — 3x more, none of it previously measured. These first values are the worst observed across two calibration runs x ~1.25; tighten them as the surfaces improve. SUBSCREENS ADDED 2026-08-22: every budget above this addition covered a ROOT screen (a tab you land on), and the hold menu's subscreens — which no root census can see — shipped two heat regressions straight through the gate (libertyLandmark's per-render triggerRepaint, fa69dba; StatsScreen's seven infinite background-position animations, ba1a3b0). Six hold-menu subscreens are now measured, but SELECTIVELY: each surface costs ~50-60s and sync-mobile runs on every push and every watcher auto-sync, so measuring all six every time would add ~5 minutes to every publish. The gate instead measures every subscreen whose OWN sources changed since its last passing measurement (zero latency on the case that actually bites, and that is exactly the Stats case), capped per run, plus one rotating stalest screen when nothing changed. State lives in .codex/thermal-subscreen-state.json.

feed._infiniteNote: The 2 are feedTitleMarquee and feedHeadlineSwap. The marquee is the title track's composited transform crawl, unfrozen for tier-ios on 2026-08-17 because freezing it clipped long titles unread. feedHeadlineSwap is the headline's title/handle trade, raised from 1 to 2 deliberately on 2026-09-04: that trade shipped as TWO opposing infinite fades (one per line) and was merged into ONE sliding track in the same commit, so this budget admits fewer animations than the feature actually ran. Both are compositor-driven transforms on a single line of type. A THIRD infinite animation here is a regression.

map._infiniteNote: Weather and other decorative effects must be fully parked after the idle acknowledgement; visible motion remains available during interaction and explicit Tour operations.
map._idleRendersNote: RAISED FROM A HARDCODED 2 ON 2026-09-03, deliberately, by the owner. Mapbox frames drawn during the 60s untouched dwell. The old 2 encoded an assumption that has stopped being true: that the board does not change while nobody is touching it. It now does. `posts` is a LIVE query, the synthetic beta cohort posts and engages continuously, and radiusDecay runs hourly against every post — so claimed territory genuinely changes shape during the dwell, and each real change MUST draw or the map is lying about who holds the ground. Measured 4 in a 60s dwell against the live cohort. 8 is 2x that headroom for a busier board, and still catches this check's entire reason for existing by a wide margin: the autonomous-rendering regressions it has caught measured 19, 22 and 43. Raise this only for the same reason — more REAL board activity — and never to quiet a renderer that is drawing on its own. The static-idle assertion, the parked-before/after check and the retained-heap budget are all untouched and remain the guards against autonomous work. Note the honest caveat: the 4 was measured before mapClaims stopped re-pushing an identical board when only a post's engagement-derived fameScore moved, so the true live number is likely lower than 4.

map-arrival._note: front=1 — the map as users actually arrive at it (tapping the map tab mounts front=1). Deliberately ARRIVAL-ONLY: the idle census belongs to the `map` surface, which uses front=0 to keep the cinematic intro out of its idle sample. Absent budgets are skipped by the checks.

profile-stats._note: Hold-menu SUBSCREEN (?view=holdmenu&holdScreen=profile-stats). Measured on the built snapshot, 8s idle census after a 36s settle: BEFORE 10 infinite animations, 793ms renderer CPU, 2592ms arrival; AFTER ba1a3b0 froze them on the tier-ios / ambient-sleep / low_power / emergency edges: 3 infinite animations, 106ms renderer CPU, 1485ms arrival. profile-stats._infiniteNote: Exactly the three .pulseRing rings on the hero: `pulse` animates transform+opacity only, so it is composited and free. Three <div className={styles.pulseRing}/> are rendered statically by StatsScreen.tsx, so this count is not data-dependent — a FOURTH infinite animation is a regression, and a background-position one is the regression this budget was written for.
profile-stats._idleNote: 106ms measured at load 11, 119 at load 36, 138 at load 105 (three samples, built snapshot). 200 = 1.9x the honest floor and 1.45x the worst-observed-under-contention, while sitting 4x below the 793ms the unfrozen shimmer cost. The three composited pulse rings are the whole of it; freezing them too would take this to its siblings' ~9ms and this budget should then be tightened.

budgets._subscreenNote: The five inert subscreens above share one budget shape because they measured the same: ZERO infinite animations and 6-9ms of renderer CPU per 8s idle census. maxLongTaskMs 150 is ~17x that floor and still 5x below the 793ms the Stats regression cost, so it catches a Stats-class repaint loop with room to spare; it is deliberately tighter than the 250ms floor the root surfaces use, because a hold-menu screen at rest should be doing NOTHING and these six prove that is achievable. maxInfiniteAnimations 0 is the primary catcher and is contention-proof: an animation count cannot inflate on a busy Mac, and the Stats regression would have failed it 7 times over. maxArrivalCpuMs 1900 = 1.25x the worst arrival observed (1517ms), matching profile-stats. It was first set to 1700 from a 1346ms worst case measured on a quiet machine; within the hour a real sync-mobile run measured profile-wallet at 1517ms at load 28, leaving only 12% margin on the noisiest quantity this gate samples (arrival inflates under contention far more than idle CPU does: the siblings ran 1074-1126ms at low load and 1474-1517ms under it). Corrected on that evidence rather than waiting for it to fail a device push. 1900 still sits well below the 2464-2760ms the actual Stats regression produced, so the arrival check keeps its catching power. Calibrated 2026-08-22 against the built snapshot, not the dev server. DEV-SERVER TRAP: these are calibrated against the BUILT snapshot, like every budget here since 2026-08-15. Run the gate ad-hoc against the 5199 dev server and the subscreen ARRIVAL check fails spuriously — Vite serves unbundled ES modules, so boot costs about twice the CPU (profile-wallet measured 1939-2010ms on 5199 against 1108-1126ms on the built bundle, while its idle CPU, animation count and WebGL count were identical). That is dev overhead, not heat that ships; do not raise the budget to accommodate it. Point POPLUR_THERMAL_BASE at a `vite preview` of a real build instead, which is what sync-mobile does.
